newsitem.title: USA: Italy's Dini says spending cuts must take place.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini says spending cuts must take place.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said Monday that his country must cut government spending, including implementing pension cuts, even if it means doing so with a different government majority.

In remarks prepared for delivery to the World Economy Laboratory conference here, Dini said "structural measures to reduce spending must be adopted even if the parliamentary majority supporting them does not fully coincide with the one that has supported the center-left government so far."
Dini said his support and that of his party for the government led by Romano Prodi was conditioned on it succeeding in achieving promised budgetary consolidation.

"If the extreme left and trade unions continue to oppose spending cuts or any change in the welfare state, the government must take the initiative and submit a bill to Parliament for which it will be possible to obtain the support of the opposition," Dini said in a text of his address.

The government led by Romano Prodi has the support of the hard left Communist Refoundation Party, which however has no seats in government. Dini's own party, Rinnovamento Italiano, fared poorly at partial local elections Sunday, with early returns showing less that one percent of total votes in its favor.

Dini said Italy had made major progress towards reaching the three percent budget deficit-to-GDP target needed to enter the European single currency. But it must now attack structural spending to ensure its sustainability and time was running short.
"The area where this can be done with the greatest long-run impact and the least social cost is the pension system" Dini said.
